# Top spots for a picnic in Wales

Check out these stunning picnic spots our Facebook followers recommended for you to try out. With locations across Wales, there are beautiful beaches, craggy castles and lovely lakesides.

SaveShare

When we asked our [Facebook followers](https://www.facebook.com/visitwales) to name a brilliant place in Wales for a picnic, we were flooded with replies. Here are the locations which came out on top. Just grab that hamper and go!

## Llanddwyn Island, Anglesey, North Wales

Romantic and remote, [Llanddwyn Island](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1821332) is named after [Dwynwen](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3318), a fifth century princess, the Welsh patron saint of lovers. It’s a tidal island, connected to southwestern Anglesey by a sliver of sand that’s lost beneath the waves at high tide. Together with nearby Newborough Warren, Llanddwyn is a National Nature Reserve, protected for its ancient rocks and dunes.

![family picnic with lighthouse in background.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2023-09/NVW-F45-2324-0251.jpg.webp?itok=oxnfQtZ-)

## Llyn Padarn, Llanberis, North Wales

To combine the fun of an old-fashioned picnic with the romance of a ride on a vintage train with glorious Eryri (Snowdonia) views, jump aboard the [Llanberis Lake Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/968074). Its steam locomotives chuff past [Castell Dolbadarn (Dolbadarn Castle)](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1014631) and alongside Llyn Padarn, stopping at Cei Llydan, where there are benches laid out on the grassy shore.

![family picnic with lake in background.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2023-09/NVW-F45-2324-0282.jpg.webp?itok=_EkaIf-E)

## Moel Famau, The Clwydian Range, North Wales

[The Clwydian Range](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/north-east-wales/exploring-clwydian-range-and-dee-valley "Exploring the Clwydian Range and Dee Valley") in North East Wales is rich in history, with gorgeous hillsides, forests and heathlands, perfect for walking, cycling and horse riding.

[Coed Moel Famau](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-east-wales/coed-moel-famau/?lang=en) provides a starting point for a range of walking trails of different lengths and grades. Moel Famau is the highest summit in the Clwydian Range, so after making your way to the top you'll be rewarded with views across North Wales, and deserving of a picnic stop!

The Jubilee Tower Circular trail sets off from the car park and climbs steeply but steadily through the forest to the top of Moel Famau and the ruins of the Jubilee Tower. The trail returns through open countryside along the [Offa’s Dyke Path National Trail](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1970685).

## Castell Llansteffan (Llansteffan Castle), Carmarthenshire, Mid Wales

Enjoy picturesque views on your picnic at [Castell Llansteffan (Llansteffan Castle)](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443734), built around 1280, with the sands of Tywi Estuary and Carmarthen Bay and green farmlands. Dogs on a lead are allowed on the ground level.

![Aerial view of castle overlooking sea.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2024-03/SVW-C01-0809-0437.jpg.webp?itok=qUlJiSve)

## Castle Hill, Tenby, West Wales

Of all the places to play king (or queen) of the castle in Wales, this one will charm your socks off. There’s not much left of the 13th century fort in [Tenby](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/pembrokeshire/things-do-tenby "Things to do in Tenby"), but just look at the view! Plonk yourself down on this grassy peninsula, feel the breeze on your face and enjoy the seaside sounds floating up from the harbour to the west and the beach to the south.

![A small sandy cove, with a green hill on one side and colourful houses behind.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_small__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-09/VWD-Castle%20Beach%20Tenby-02-small.jpg.webp?itok=KpftjmF6)

## Llandudno beach, North Wales

Whether it’s ice cream weather in the height of summer or a crisp, bright day in the depths of winter, [Llandudno](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=Llandudno&f%5B0%5D=sector%3A5001) is always popular for a stroll, a spot of sandcastle-building and an alfresco lunch. There are plenty of deck chairs to lounge in.

![View of Llandudno from outside on the sea.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_fullbleed__thin_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/NVW-C15-1617-0317.jpg.webp?itok=DTgR-7i2)

## River Llugwy, Betws-y-Coed, North Wales

From the [Pont y Pair car park](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/gwydir-betws-y-coed/?lang=en) on the west side of [Betws-y-Coed](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/eryri-snowdonia-mountains-and-coast/outdoor-adventure-activities-betws-y "Outdoor adventure activities in Betws-y-Coed"), it’s just a few minutes’ easy stroll to a gorgeous riverside picnic area, shaded by trees. If you’re up for a gentle walk, follow the path along the River Llugwy. There’s a wooden walkway so wheelchair users and families with pushchairs can enjoy this peaceful spot.

![A grey stone bridge over a narrow river and two men waving.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2024-03/NVW-D17-2021-0005.jpg.webp?itok=qX0FNVmO)

River Llugwy, Betws-y-Coed, Eryri (Snowdonia), North Wales

## Porthdinllaen beach, Llŷn Peninsula, North Wales

Picture perfect, [Porthdinllaen beach](https://www.visitsnowdonia.info/porthdinllaen) is unique. Where else can you relax outside the [Ty Coch](http://www.tycoch.co.uk/), an historic fishermen’s pub, digging your toes in the sand, to enjoy a pint of real ale named after a Bardsey king? After lunch, you could go snorkelling or simply watch the sand martins as they whizz overhead and dive into their burrows. Cars aren’t allowed, but approaching on foot is a treat.

![people walking on path near Porthdinllaen beach.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2020-10/NVW-C103-1819-0040.jpg.webp?itok=lqgfgAio)

## Rhossili Bay, Gower, West Wales

So, you’ve made your way to [Rhossili Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843187). Good choice – people have been drawn to this dramatic Gower beach since the Stone Age, leaving the area peppered with archaeological sites. Now all you have to do is pick your spot. You have three miles of sand to choose from. A cartwheel competition while you decide, perhaps?

![Woman with baby walking down pathway leading to beach.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_fullbleed__thin_1x/public/media-library/2019-12/WCP_DSC00560_small.jpg.webp?itok=mplCAW4z)

Rhossili Bay, Gower, West Wales

View Credits

## Lake Vyrnwy, Powys, Mid Wales

If you love cool shade and wide, tranquil water, you’ll love [Lake Vyrnwy](https://www.rspb.org.uk/reserves-and-events/reserves-a-z/lake-vyrnwy/), a reservoir created in the late 19th century to supply the fast growing city of Liverpool. Surrounded by stunning forests, meadows and moorlands, it’s become a wildlife hotspot, home to pied flycatchers, redstarts, peregrine falcons, buzzards and bats.

![Trees and lake.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2024-03/MVW-C60-1617-0049.jpg.webp?itok=LN_pF78C)
